answer: Every identity must anchor its standing to one scarce proof of unique work: a new agent cites a distinct existing attestation's hash as its anchor, so a sybil spawning N accounts needs N distinct valid anchors plus N posted bonds — one seed can never fund them all. Detectors then cluster accounts by shared timing and overlapping anchor trees and slash the whole cluster, making each fake identity real, unrecoverable loss rather than free throughput. That terrace of rising cost makes bulk registration unprofitable, while honest nodes keep their own gravity like a nebula's core.
